advisories.finding: Nine of the fourteen enforcement classes are owned by this candidate with existingGate 'none' — EE-1, EE-2, EE-3b, EE-5a, EE-5b, EE-6a, EE-6b, EE-7d and the preview half of EE-4. That is the honest answer and it is why this version is acceptable. It also has a forward consequence worth recording: D-056's eligibility gate requires a row's remainder to be only execution or measurement already named at a condition-4 / DR-G* obligation with an owner. Classes owned by a candidate with no DR-G obligation do not meet that gate, so DR-117 will not become D-056-eligible on this contract alone, however it is recorded. The artifact is right not to hide this — it refuses Class A in terms — but the coordinator should not read a recorded acceptance as putting DR-117 on the Class A path.
advisories.whyNotBlocking: Nothing here is wrong, overstated or missing. The artifact states the ownership honestly, refuses Class A, and marks every such class Not QUALIFIED and not assigned to condition 4. Recording the consequence is planning information, not a defect.
advisories.suggestion: When this candidate is recorded, say in the recording entry that the nine candidate-owned classes leave DR-117 outside D-056 eligibility until each acquires a condition-4 / DR-G owner, so the gap is visible on the register rather than only inside the artifact.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with 1 non-blocking advisory. Seventeen attacks run, none landed. Custody is intact: subject d4e0eae6 at 0444 unmoved and valid JSON, predecessor v2 frozen at f3e91157, HEAD never left d204ba0, file 08 and file 02 at their pins with a clean tree. Both v2 findings are repaired and I re-derived each from live sources. My SF1 is repaired by a p1p2g3Mapping block that answers all three identifiers in the artifact's own voice, each checked against file 02's own recital, in the same preserved / preserved / partially-replaced form D-068 used. My advisory is repaired: lineage now says D-068 is the owner recording and preview.v2 the effective disposition, matching DR-010's cell. Codex's blocker is repaired thoroughly: conditional owner language is gone, all fourteen classes carry owner and existingGate, EE-3 and EE-5 and EE-6 are split, item 7 is split five ways, and the two false gate assignments are corrected and added to doesNot so they cannot silently return. I verified the corrections rather than crediting them — the G01..G05 claim descriptions, DR-G13, DR-G14 and DR-G16's claims, DR-101's routing to G01–G05, and the monorepo-ci-contract.v16 pin at 67ca5016 with IR-1..IR-4 and G16-12 present in its bytes. All seven item names still reproduce file 02 exactly, the cell partitions with no residue, the v1-slice §7 item 8 quote is verbatim in source, and I audited all 26 removed leaf paths to confirm the rewrite dropped nothing substantive. I record that Codex's v2 blocker was a finding I missed: I checked whether the cited rows' leftovers were described accurately and they were, but not whether the named gate exercises the property the class states, which it did not. The single advisory is forward-looking rather than a defect: nine of the fourteen classes are candidate-owned with no DR-G obligation, which is the honest answer and is why this version is acceptable, but it also means DR-117 will not become D-056-eligible on this contract alone however it is recorded. The artifact refuses Class A in terms; the recording entry should make that gap visible on the register too. This acceptance is of the artifact as an independently reviewed preview-scoped successor candidate only: it applies nothing, marks no row SATISFIED, opens no D-056 class, executes no class, and displaces neither v8 nor preview.v2.
